topic: Forgot a newly changed iPhone passcode: check previous-passcode recovery before erasing

decisions: Direct answer prioritizes eligibility and the previous-passcode route before destructive recovery. A decorative 72-hour/old-code/new-code diagram contains no input fields.

Software and model distinctions: iOS 17+ feature versus 15.2/16 erasing option; Face ID versus Touch ID passcode settings; Apple Account/Screen Time/Activation Lock distinguished from device unlock code.

Attempt-limit warning appears before steps; guide starts at the displayed recovery choice and does not reproduce a deliberate five-failure recipe. Uncertain attempt history, declined previous code or missing choices get a stopping point.
Explain early expiry and one-time use without claiming a specific reason for rejection. Expire Previous Passcode Now discussed only after regaining access and confirming new code.

Differentiate successful non-erasing Passcode Reset from Start iPhone Reset/Erase iPhone/computer Restore. eSIM and account prerequisites explained before any later erase; computer button sequence linked rather than reproduced.
After regained access, finish a backup and verify its date. While locked out, preserve existing backups and separately synced data without promising a new backup or recovery of unsaved files.
Two native disclosures for old-code expiry and erase-only choices; no article JavaScript, code-collection form, ads, tracking or new affiliate placement.

Source-based organization attribution; no invented physical recovery test, expertise or business promise. Creation/publication/review metadata October 31; no claim source documents were updated today.
Preserve corrected hours and all six business-hours regression tests. No Mac or other repository, accounts/security/hosting changes or external outreach.
